clusters.text: The author, a 62-year-old woman with a nursing master's degree, will vote Republican for every office on the ballot.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim is an unattributed first-person statement about a private person's age, education and future vote. I found no letter, op-ed or post that identifies the author, and no record or poll release that could confirm any of those details. The searches returned only race context: 
Patrick won his March primary outright and Goodwin took the Democratic nomination in May
 (Texas Tribune). The Houston Chronicle and Austin American-Statesman editorial boards have also endorsed Goodwin. None of this speaks to this author's age, degree or ballot choices. A stated intention to vote also can't be checked, because ballots are secret and the vote hasn't happened yet. The claim is neither confirmed nor contradicted.

clusters.text: A UT poll shows Vikki Goodwin leading Dan Patrick 49% to 46% in the Lieutenant Governor race.
clusters.verdict_basis: The UT/Texas Politics Project's own release of Oct. 14, 2026 lists the Lt. Governor result as Patrick 46%, Goodwin 49%, Libertarian Anthony Cristo 2%, Green Party candidate Kevin McCormick 1%, and "someone else" 2%. The poll surveyed 1,200 registered voters from Sept. 25 to Oct. 5, with a ±2.83-point margin of error. The Texas Tribune, KXAN and WFAA all report the same 49%–46% figure. The claim's numbers and attribution are accurate. One caveat is that the 3-point gap is within the poll's margin of error for likely voters. The UT release itself describes Democratic leads as narrow and within that margin, and the Tribune calls them "razor-thin." The claim doesn't say otherwise, so I don't treat it as misleading.
